---
title: FAQ
description: Common questions about Wakaru.
---

## How is Wakaru different from a formatter or beautifier?

A formatter changes whitespace and layout. Wakaru also recovers modern
syntax, removes recognized helpers, and splits bundles into modules.
See [What is Wakaru](/what-is-wakaru) for a before-and-after example.

## How do I unminify JavaScript?

Run `npx wakaru input.js -o output.js`, or paste the code into the
[playground](https://wakarujs.com/playground/). See
[Unminify a file](/guides/unminify-a-file) for output options and name recovery.

## How do I decompile a webpack bundle?

Run `npx wakaru bundle.js --unpack -o out/`. For a build with multiple chunks,
pass them together. [Unpack a bundle](/guides/unpack-a-bundle) explains how to
choose the inputs, and [Read an unpacked bundle](/guides/read-an-unpacked-bundle)
shows how to find the code you need afterward.

## Can I run the recovered code as an application?

It is possible. Start with `--level minimal` to prioritize preserving the
input's behavior. Wakaru aims to produce working code, but cannot guarantee
that every case will run correctly. You may also need to restore dependencies,
assets, and build configuration. See [Rewrite levels](/guides/rewrite-levels).

## Can Wakaru extract JavaScript from a Bun single-file executable?

Yes. Run `npx wakaru ./compiled-app --unpack -o out/`. Wakaru reads the
embedded JavaScript without running the executable. To extract assets too,
see [Bun single-file executable](/guides/bun-single-file-executable).

## Can Wakaru deobfuscate JavaScript?

Wakaru focuses on minifier and transpiler output. Deliberately obfuscated
code needs a dedicated tool first. See [Obfuscated code](/guides/obfuscated-code)
for how to recognize it and combine tools.

## Can it recover original variable names?

When a source map retains the original names, Wakaru can recover them.
Without one, some names can be inferred from the code, but most mangled
locals stay short. See [Source maps](/guides/source-maps) for name recovery
and extracting original files, or [Variable names](/guides/unminify-a-file#variable-names)
for other options.

## Is the output guaranteed to behave the same?

Not for every input. Wakaru tests semantic preservation, and
[rewrite levels](/guides/rewrite-levels) let you choose how far recovery goes.
Use `minimal` when behavioral fidelity matters most. See
[Correctness](/project/correctness) for what the tests measure.

## Does it run in the browser?

Yes. The [playground](https://wakarujs.com/playground/) processes code locally
in your browser. Use the CLI to unpack bundles or work with multiple files.
See [Playground](/guides/playground) for the available modes.
